replication.target_description: Participants’ foot shaking in the presence of a confederate engaging in foot shaking. Main analysis of 14 participants; repeated-measures interaction with confederate behavior order, adjusting baseline.

n.exclusions: From recruited N = 35: technical recording problems, real-purpose awareness, and suspected confederate awareness; main analysis restricted to those passing exclusion criteria. Exploratory sample is separate.
n.quote: The main analysis only included the data of the fourteen participants, which passed the exclusion criteria.

p.location: supplied p. 30; §5.4.2 Behavioral mannerisms, paragraph beginning “The main analysis showed”
p.quote: there was no significant interaction between foot shaking and the confederate’s behavior Wilks λ = .83, F(1, 10) = 2.06, p = .182, η2 = .171

reported_success.quote: However, the explorative analysis as well as the non-parametric test revealed a significant interaction effect for foot shaking in the expected direction, which indicates that the non-detection of the effect could have been the result of the exclusion criteria and the hence limited power.

notes: Replication DOCX is BA_OSF.docx from the named OSF project; its reference list identifies Förster (2022), The Chameleon Effect: A Replication Study. Printed metric retained. Primary planned main analysis selected, not exploratory or outlier sensitivity analyses. Original primary scanned PDF title and authors verified; statistic quotes visually checked against PDF page 7 to correct OCR punctuation. Original simple effects for face rubbing and foot shaking are distinct from the omnibus interaction F(1, 34) = 9.36, p = .004. Replication tests are the corresponding outcome-specific interactions across session and confederate order. DOCX pagination was not reconstructed; section and paragraph provide exact text locations. Replication main analysis did not confirm foot shaking; authors describe positive exploratory and non-parametric evidence, hence mixed narrative verdict.
